amendments.because: The owner decided on 2026-10-01 that tests don't count toward the five-file fix limit, after most allowances that day were for tests changing with the code
amendments.done_when: The fix-size limit (the commit hook and close) doesn't count files whose content is exactly what forge sync writes for this repo; any other change to them, and every other file, still counts. A command-level test commits an upgrade fix whose only code changes are forge sync's output (accepted without an allowance) and one that also edits a synced file by hand beyond sync's output (counted).

done_when: The fix-size limit (the commit hook and close) counts only non-test code files: it doesn't count test files (the repo's test paths Forge already recognises) or files whose content is exactly what forge sync writes for this repo; any other change to a synced file, and every other code file, still counts, and the interface rule is unchanged. Command-level tests: an upgrade fix whose only code changes are forge sync's output closes without an allowance; one that also hand-edits a synced file is counted; a fix with four source files and three test files commits without an allowance.

findings.body: The new test exercises commits and pushes, but never close or its required PR check. Removing the exemption at prcheck.py:209–216 would leave this regression test passing. Existing upgrade coverage in tests/test_upgrade_synced.py:30 and tests/test_upgrade_check.py:181 supplies allow_large, which bypasses the changed limit. Add command-level coverage without an allowance that closes a sync-only fix and verifies that a hand-edited synced file plus five ordinary code files is counted and refused by the real PR-check command.
findings.title: Not done: A command-level close test proves sync output is exempt and hand edits count

findings.body: The archive is not an exact copy of the baseline: [Git applies export-ignore and export-subst](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-archive#_attributes). For example, if a client excludes .claude/settings.json from exports, the temporary tree loses its existing permissions. sync._hooks (sync.py:169–189) consequently computes different output from a real sync over that baseline. With five ordinary code changes, a correctly synced settings file is then counted as a sixth file and refused; conversely, manually removing the preserved settings can match the incorrect expected output and become exempt. Materialize the baseline without export transformations.
findings.title: Preserve baseline files when computing sync output

why: An upgrade fix can't commit without the owner's allowance because forge sync's own output (host hooks, skills and eleven subagent roles per tool) counts toward the five-code-file fix limit
